task.title: Fit an image in its box
task.shortdesc: When the box of an image has another proportion than the image, you choose how the image fills it. You can also turn an image and choose how its pixels are drawn.

step.cmd: Choose how the image fills the box

info.p: The object-fit property applies when you set both the width and the height of the image, and they do not have the proportion of the image. These are its values:

ul.li: fill is the initial value. The image is stretched to the box, and its proportions change.
contain scales the image as large as it can be and still fit in the box. Part of the box can stay empty.
cover scales the image as small as it can be and still cover the box. Part of the image is cut.
none keeps the natural size of the image.
scale-down is the smaller result of none and contain, so an image is never enlarged.

image.alt: Five square boxes that show the same wide picture. With fill it is stretched. With contain it fits, with empty space above and below. With cover it fills the box and its sides are cut. With none and with scale-down it has its natural size, in the middle of the box.

step.cmd: Position the image in the box

info.p: When the image does not fill the box, object-position decides where it goes. It takes the values of background-position: keywords, lengths and percentages. The initial value is 50% 50%, the center of the box.
This photo fills its box, and the part that is cut comes from the bottom of the picture.

Cameras store a photo in the same way for every position and write in the file how to turn it. The image-orientation property decides what CSSMedia does with that. The initial value, from-image, turns the image as the file says. A quarter turn swaps the width and the height of the natural size. Other values:

ul.li: none shows the image as it is stored.
An angle, such as 90deg, turns the image by that angle, rounded to a multiple of 90 degrees. It replaces what the file says.
flip mirrors the image, after the turn. It can follow an angle.

step.cmd: Choose how the pixels are drawn

info.p: When an image is shown larger than its pixels, image-rendering decides how the PDF viewer fills the space between them:

ul.li: auto is the initial value. smooth and high-quality do the same. They ask the viewer to smooth the image.
crisp-edges asks the viewer not to blend the colors of the pixels.
pixelated enlarges the image by whole multiples of its pixels, so that each pixel becomes a sharp square. Use it for small images such as bar codes.

info.note: A PDF does not move, so the property image-animation has no effect.
